hypothesis.title: Checkout memory leak causing OOMKills and 10% error rate
hypothesis.summary: Checkout is experiencing a memory leak that began ~28 minutes before the alert. Heap usage climbed above 90% after full GC, leading to repeated OOMKills (5 restarts) and a crash loop. Each OOM restart causes in-flight requests to fail with "fatal error: runtime: out of memory", driving the error rate from 0.4% to 10%. The memory pressure predates the recent payment deploy by 18 minutes, ruling out that change as the cause.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on checkout with a 10% error rate. The trace analysis shows 94% of failing traces end in checkout itself, with the deepest error being "fatal error: runtime: out of memory". The checkout pod (checkout-fdeb62aa-da730) has been OOMKilled 5 times and is in a BackOff restart loop. Checkout logs show 360 warnings of "heap usage above 90% after full GC" starting 28 minutes before the alert, followed by 5 "fatal error: runtime: out of memory" errors starting 24 minutes before the alert. Memory utilization metrics show checkout spiked to 93.2% around 25 minutes before the alert, with a sawtooth pattern consistent with OOM restarts. The payment 1.9.0→1.9.1 deploy 6 minutes before the alert is a red herring: payment's own metrics are healthy (0.4% error rate, 46ms p95 latency, stable CPU/memory), and the checkout memory pressure began 24 minutes before the alert—18 minutes before the payment deploy. The memory growth pattern and repeated OOMKills point to a memory leak in checkout itself, not a bad deploy elsewhere.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Confirms checkout pod has been OOMKilled 5 times, the direct mechanism causing the errors.
Shows 5 fatal OOM errors in checkout starting 24 minutes before the alert, matching the trace error messages.
360 warnings of heap usage above 90% after full GC starting 28 minutes before alert indicate memory leak and GC pressure before OOMKills.
Memory spiked to 93.2% at -25m and shows sawtooth pattern consistent with leak-induced OOM restarts.
Failing trace shows the error originates in checkout's own span with 'fatal error: runtime: out of memory'.
Payment deploy at -6m is a red herring: checkout memory pressure began at -28m, 22 minutes earlier, and payment metrics are healthy.

suggested_actions.title: Restart checkout deployment to temporarily restore service
suggested_actions.rationale: Clears the accumulated memory and stops the OOM crash loop. This is the safest immediate mitigation per runbook RB-oom.

suggested_actions.title: Increase checkout memory limit to buy time for investigation
suggested_actions.rationale: If the leak rate is slow, raising the limit can extend time between OOMs while root cause is investigated.

suggested_actions.title: Capture heap dump before next OOM for leak analysis
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo exec -it deployment/checkout -- curl -o /tmp/heap.prof http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap
suggested_actions.rationale: Collect memory profile to identify which objects/code paths are leaking. Requires the pod to be running and pprof endpoint available.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Payment 1.9.1 deployed only 6 minutes before the alert, but checkout memory pressure and OOM errors began 24 minutes before the alert (18 minutes before the payment deploy). Payment's own metrics are healthy with 0.4% error rate and stable latency, and postmortem PM-2026-01-20 describes payment errors manifesting in payment's own metrics, not just checkout.
